policy: Original courses and exams remain unchanged. Case content is fictional, decision assessments are browser-local, and written work requires independent expert review.

cases.title: Linux Audit Trail — Unexpected Configuration Change
cases.scope: An authorized learner investigates a synthetic file-change alert inside a disposable Linux workspace. The objective is evidence preservation and defensible conclusions, not exploitation.

stages.title: Establish the baseline
stages.evidence: Training directory /home/student/lab. The app.conf file existed at 08:00 and was last modified at 09:14. An operator says the app was 'hacked'.

decisions.prompt: What can you conclude from the timestamp?
options: An unexpected modification is recorded; cause is unknown
decisions.explanation: A changed timestamp is an observation, not attribution.

decisions.prompt: Which evidence should you capture first?
options: Current file metadata and content hash with acquisition time
Rewrite the file to an earlier version immediately
decisions.explanation: Capture non-destructive evidence before applying changes.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Correlate records
stages.evidence: 09:10 approved maintenance CHG-21. 09:14 file hash changes. 09:14 svc-update process reads the file. No actor authentication evidence is supplied.

decisions.prompt: How should the change ticket be interpreted?
options: Corroborating context, not proof this modification was authorized
decisions.explanation: Change-window overlap is relevant but does not establish authorization of a specific action.

decisions.prompt: Which missing artifact most directly helps attribution?
options: Process ancestry and approved deployment execution record
decisions.explanation: Process and workload provenance help determine which actor caused a change.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Plan remediation
stages.evidence: The current config contains 'debug=true' but the approved baseline requires 'debug=false'. Recovery has not been authorized.

decisions.prompt: What is the appropriate next step?
options: Request approval and document rollback plus verification
decisions.explanation: Changes to a system should be approved and reversible.

decisions.prompt: What verification is needed after an approved fix?
options: Config content, hash and service health
A screenshot of a login page
decisions.explanation: Check file state and the effect on the service.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Close with uncertainty
stages.evidence: After an approved configuration correction, the service reports healthy; the identity behind the original change remains uncertain.

options: The service is recovered, while attribution remains unresolved
decisions.explanation: Operational recovery and attribution are separate.

options: Review deployment credentials, access logs and change controls
decisions.explanation: Remaining gaps should have accountable owners and specific evidence requests.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: Workstation Boot Failure — Hardware Versus OS
cases.scope: A repair technician is authorized to inspect a fictional training computer, but not to replace components until diagnostic evidence is reviewed.

stages.title: Classify the symptom
stages.evidence: Power light on, fan spins, no BIOS logo, POST memory code appears. Storage test not yet available.

decisions.explanation: A POST fault arises before operating-system loading.

decisions.prompt: What is a safe first observation?
options: Record POST code and known hardware configuration
decisions.explanation: Record the symptom before modifying the system.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Compare component evidence
stages.evidence: Approved repeat memory test reports errors for DIMM B2. SSD has no critical warning. Errors reproduce when the module is reinstalled in the same slot.

options: Nothing; the module is proven faulty
The error is definitely a virus
Whether the module or slot is defective
decisions.explanation: One slot/module combination does not discriminate between module and socket.

options: Change one variable by trying the same module in an approved alternate slot
decisions.explanation: Controlled isolation is stronger than swapping unrelated parts.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Authorize correction
stages.evidence: A repair window and ESD procedure are approved. The fault follows the module to another approved slot.

decisions.prompt: Which component is now most suspect?
decisions.explanation: A traveling fault supports a module hypothesis.

options: Pretest, authorization, part identification, action and posttest
decisions.explanation: Traceability matters in technical service operations.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Retest and close
stages.evidence: Replacement memory passes a repeat test and workstation starts repeatedly. No extended stress test has been completed.

decisions.prompt: What should the final report state?
options: Diagnostic tests passed; long-term stability still needs monitoring
decisions.explanation: Pass results support improvement without proving future infallibility.

options: Record a monitoring plan and asset information
decisions.explanation: Retain the complete service record.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: Network Outage — DNS and Routing in Sequence
cases.scope: A fictional internal application is unreachable by hostname. The scope permits read-only checks and approved changes within training network 10.40.0.0/24.

stages.title: Map the reachability layers
stages.evidence: Client IP 10.40.0.20/24; expected server 10.40.0.80. DNS resolves app.lab.example to 10.40.0.81. Direct HTTP to 10.40.0.80 returns 200.

decisions.explanation: Name resolution is inconsistent with the expected service IP.

decisions.prompt: Which safe read-only comparison is best?
options: Check DNS answer and direct-IP HTTP separately
decisions.explanation: Layer-separated checks reduce false conclusions.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Reassess after correction
stages.evidence: An approved DNS correction now resolves 10.40.0.80, but a second client still fails because it has a route for 10.40.0.0/24 via the wrong adapter.

options: The remaining issue is client-specific routing
decisions.explanation: Different clients can suffer distinct faults.

decisions.prompt: Which observation best supports the routing hypothesis?
options: ip route get 10.40.0.80 on the affected client
decisions.explanation: Routing decisions are the relevant layer.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Plan limited recovery
stages.evidence: The authorized network engineer approves correcting the affected client's static route, with a rollback.

options: Change only the scoped client route and retain previous setting
Bridge the vulnerable lab to the office LAN
decisions.explanation: Use minimum-scope changes and preserve isolation.

options: Routing decision, DNS answer and successful application transaction
decisions.explanation: Service recovery requires multiple independent checks.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Report findings
stages.evidence: DNS and a bad client route were both corrected. No user impact records exist for the outage interval.

options: Both faults were addressed; impact duration remains uncertain
A single person intentionally caused both faults
decisions.explanation: Separate verified fixes from unmeasured impact and attribution.

options: Time-series service availability and user transaction logs
A screenshot of Task Manager only
decisions.explanation: Recover measurable business impact from independent logs.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: SOC Incident — Approved Deployment or Credential Abuse?
cases.scope: Analyze synthetic identity logs, endpoint inventory and change approval. No access to real accounts or production systems is required.

stages.title: Initial detection
stages.evidence: svc-release logs in from device D-9 at 09:12. Anomaly score 72. Successful sign-in with no verified device owner.

options: Possible anomalous identity event, attribution unknown
decisions.explanation: Anomaly detection flags a question for investigation.

decisions.prompt: What is the correct triage action?
options: Record identity, source and exact timestamp before interpreting
decisions.explanation: Preserve primary facts.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Evidence correlation
stages.evidence: CHG-42 permits deployment 09:00–09:20. Pipeline-8 executed at 09:13. D-9 is not in the registered device inventory.

options: An overlapping change window, not validated device ownership
decisions.explanation: Approved changes can coexist with misuse.

decisions.prompt: Which record most improves the assessment?
options: Signed pipeline provenance and device ownership
decisions.explanation: Investigate the event's chain of identity and execution.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Containment decision
stages.evidence: No malicious action has been proven. The identity has broad privileges and is still active; security lead approves a scoped privilege review.

options: Review token scope and rotate/revoke if approved by incident owner
Publish credentials in an incident thread
decisions.explanation: Containment should match evidence and approvals, with attention to service continuity.

decisions.prompt: What information belongs in the change plan?
options: Owners, downtime risk, fallback, monitoring and validation
decisions.explanation: Scoped changes still need operational controls.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Close or escalate
stages.evidence: Deployment records validate an expected job, but D-9 ownership remains unresolved and token audience logs are missing.

options: Document open attribution gap and follow-up owner
decisions.explanation: Residual uncertainty warrants specific follow-up rather than false closure.

decisions.prompt: What should the final report explicitly separate?
options: Observed activity, hypotheses, and unresolved evidence
decisions.explanation: Separation of observation and interpretation underpins accurate SOC reporting.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: Web Assessment — Authorization and Regression
cases.scope: The assessment targets only a synthetic web application on a privately isolated lab. A trainee must document object authorization and patch verification.

stages.title: Define permitted behavior
stages.evidence: Policy: guest can view public profile 101, owner can view private account 102. Guest GET /account/102 returns HTTP 200 with private fields.

decisions.explanation: The endpoint disclosed a protected object to an unauthorized role.

options: Record role, object, HTTP status and response fields
Only report a feeling that it is insecure
decisions.explanation: A high-quality finding describes a controlled request and result.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Compare authorized behavior
stages.evidence: Owner GET /account/102 returns HTTP 200. Guest GET /account/101 returns HTTP 200. No production identity authentication exists in this fictional training service.

options: The mock as= role selector is not production authentication
The role selector proves secure identities
The application is a real bank
decisions.explanation: The training model focuses on authorization logic rather than real login security.

decisions.prompt: Which baseline is essential before remediation?
decisions.explanation: Positive baselines protect expected functionality.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Implement the check
stages.evidence: A code review proposes an owner check at the server endpoint. The UI will still display the private-account link in a training navigation menu.

decisions.prompt: Is UI hiding an adequate substitute?
options: Yes, because users cannot click the link
No; enforce authorization for each protected object on the server
Yes, if the page uses dark mode
decisions.explanation: Authorization must be decided by the server.

decisions.prompt: Which result is required after patch?
options: Guest gets 403 and owner still gets 200
decisions.explanation: A denial alone is not enough if legitimate use also breaks.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Write the finding
stages.evidence: The patched mode returns expected HTTP results. The trainee has not checked tokens, session expiry, or authorization for other endpoints.

options: All web app security issues are gone
This scoped object authorization case now passes defined regression checks
decisions.explanation: A specific fix does not justify global security claims.

decisions.prompt: What should be recorded as limitations?
options: Untested endpoints and absence of real authentication
decisions.explanation: An honest report identifies what wasn't tested.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: VM Isolation — Unauthorized Bridge and Capacity
cases.scope: A fictional investigator VM and target VM must run only on an internal virtual switch. No cloud services or physical router changes are in scope.

stages.title: Preflight resources
stages.evidence: Host RAM 16 GiB; OS baseline 5 GiB; guests requested 6 GiB, 4 GiB and 2 GiB. Before hypervisor overhead, allocations total 17 GiB.

options: Combined nominal memory demand exceeds physical RAM
All VMs have infinite shared RAM
The CPU speed is the only issue
decisions.explanation: Guest memory plus host baseline exceeds installed memory.

options: Reduce simultaneous workloads while preserving host overhead
decisions.explanation: Capacity planning must reserve host and hypervisor resources.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Check lab boundaries
stages.evidence: Training target VM uses a bridged adapter and has default route 192.168.1.1. Intended state is internal-only AcademyLab, private 10.40.0.0/24.

options: The target must already be compromised
decisions.explanation: A bridge can place the intentionally vulnerable VM on the real physical network.

options: Stop the vulnerable service and correct VM adapter configuration
decisions.explanation: Do not start vulnerable services until the network boundary is verified.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Reconfigure safely
stages.evidence: The trainee disconnects extra adapters, uses an internal switch, removes external default gateway and snapshots the clean lab.

options: Both guests' addresses/routes and hypervisor adapter settings
decisions.explanation: Host-side and guest-side configurations must match.

options: Whether external paths remain due to hypervisor or host configuration
Whether a laptop has a trackpad
decisions.explanation: Configuration review alone is not a complete security audit.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Service acceptance
stages.evidence: The target accepts only the documented investigator IP. A separate login mechanism is not implemented.

options: A fixed source-IP check substitutes for real authentication
This is a limited lab guard, not robust identity authentication
decisions.explanation: Source-IP controls have limitations and must be layered with isolation.

decisions.prompt: What is the next engineering requirement?
options: Independent VM/hypervisor acceptance and access-control review
decisions.explanation: A secure workflow needs verified boundaries and controls.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: Detection Engineering — False-Positive Reduction
cases.scope: An advanced analyst evaluates a fictional detection rule using 100 labeled events; the objective is justified tuning and rollback.

stages.title: Measure baseline
stages.evidence: TP=9; FP=15; FN=6; TN=70. Alerts fired on 24 events. Total labeled events 100.

decisions.explanation: Precision = TP/(TP+FP) = 9/24 = 37.5%.
Recall = TP/(TP+FN) = 9/15 = 60%.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Propose tuning
stages.evidence: An engineer wants to filter all service account events, which would cut false positives but also remove detection of some true incidents.

options: Missed incidents may rise as false positives fall
decisions.explanation: Optimization must consider false negatives, not just alert volume.

options: Independent holdout labels and operational impact
Only the training set used to tune the rule
decisions.explanation: Holdout performance reduces overfitting risk.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Assess changed candidate
stages.evidence: Candidate on a held-out labeled dataset: TP=12, FP=8, FN=3, TN=77. This dataset has 100 events with 15 actual incidents.
stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Production decision
stages.evidence: Candidate looks better on this holdout but deployment requires monitoring, sign-off and rollback. Data distributions can shift.

options: Controlled rollout with owner, thresholds, rollback and monitoring
Treat held-out results as a future guarantee
decisions.explanation: Positive retrospective evidence still needs production safeguards.

decisions.prompt: What goes in the final report?
options: Sample definitions, baselines, error impact and residual uncertainty
decisions.explanation: Explain limitations and the missed incident trade-off.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

cases.title: Executive Capstone — Multi-Cause Enterprise Outage
cases.scope: A fictional multinational enterprise experiences concurrent DNS failures, application capacity pressure and a privileged identity anomaly. Scope is analysis, not production operations.

stages.title: Build an evidence timeline
stages.evidence: 09:10 approved routing change. 09:14 DNS failures 72%. 09:16 HTTP 503 failures 24%; queue depth 800. 09:17 service account anomaly.

options: Multiple concurrent observations, causes not yet established
One actor definitively caused all faults
decisions.explanation: Time correlation does not prove causation.

options: Source, timestamp, confidence and hypothesis for each event
decisions.explanation: Provenance allows audit and revision of conclusions.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Inspect independent signals
stages.evidence: Routing rollback reduces resolver failures to 0.5%. HTTP 503 rate remains 23%, and queue depth is 790. Identity anomaly still lacks actor attribution.

options: Resolver improved but application service remains degraded
decisions.explanation: Metrics show independent residual faults.

decisions.prompt: What is the next appropriate investigation?
options: Application capacity and dependencies, plus separate identity evidence
decisions.explanation: Different layers require independent tests.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Plan approved remediation
stages.evidence: The application owner approves a reversible capacity adjustment. Security lead requests token-audience logs but cannot yet attribute the sign-in.

options: Implement scoped change, monitor service metrics, and keep identity inquiry open
Use the identity anomaly to name a suspect
decisions.explanation: Operational repair must not imply identity attribution.

decisions.prompt: What is a suitable recovery test?
options: DNS health, HTTP errors, queue depth and successful business transaction
decisions.explanation: Validate end-to-end service, not one layer.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.

stages.title: Defend executive conclusion
stages.evidence: Post-adjustment: DNS errors 0.5%; HTTP 503 errors 0.4%; queue depth 15. Synthetic business transactions succeed. Identity audit remains incomplete.

options: Service metrics recovered; identity investigation and monitoring continue
decisions.explanation: Communicate recovery and residual risks separately.

decisions.prompt: What should remain in the final handoff?
options: Owners, open questions, monitoring thresholds and independent review needs
decisions.explanation: An accountable handoff makes remaining risk actionable.

stages.reflectionPrompt: Document the observed evidence, what is uncertain, why your chosen action fits the scope, and a concrete test that would prove or disprove the working hypothesis.
